question: Should content-verified Android APKs be an explicitly allowed host-local attachment type when `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` is disabled?
rationale: The patch is mechanically narrow and rejects extension-only spoofing, but it intentionally expands the host-read attachment policy to an installable package format; that policy boundary needs owner intent rather than automated inference.

options.title: Accept verified APKs
options.body: Treat APKs with verified Android ZIP entries as archive-equivalent host-local documents and proceed after current-head Telegram proof is supplied.

options.title: Keep the existing boundary
options.body: Do not allow APK MIME values through host-read sends and close the feature direction while retaining existing archive behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept verified APKs
recommendation.body: Treat APKs with verified Android ZIP entries as archive-equivalent host-local documents and proceed after current-head Telegram proof is supplied.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature-history evidence makes this the strongest routing candidate for the host-read media policy boundary.
